title: Australia Visa Biometrics Start for India: Five Checks Before You Book
excerpt: New Australian visa applications lodged in India from October 26 may require fingerprints and a facial image. The letter, the AUI code and your passport decide whether you use the free Immi App or visit a collection centre.
body:
• Australia expanded biometrics to visa applicants in India from October 26, 2026: some applicants must now provide fingerprints and a facial image, according to the Australian High Commission in New Delhi.
  • Reader action: do not book anything before Home Affairs writes to you — wait for the official biometrics requirement letter by email, then check whether your Visa Lodgement Number starts with AUI.
  • An AUI number means you may use the free Australian Immi App; any other number means an in-person visit to one of 16 VFS Global collection centres in India, with a service fee.
  • Only applications lodged on or after October 26 are affected. Earlier applications and visas already granted are not, and processing times are not expected to change if biometrics are completed promptly.

Australia has added a biometrics step for visa applicants in India. From October 26, 2026, people lodging a new Australian visa application in India may be required to provide biometrics — fingerprints and a facial image — the Australian High Commission in India said in a statement dated October 26. The expansion brings India into a programme Australia already runs in nearly 60 countries, and it applies across visitor, student, work and other visa applications lodged from that date. It is separate from Australia's recent student visa tightening, which we covered in Australia Tightens Student Visa Rules — this change is about identity verification, not eligibility criteria.

Check One: Are You Even in Scope?

The first check is the lodgement date. The new requirements apply only to applications lodged on or after October 26, 2026, according to the High Commission. Applications submitted before that date are not affected, and neither are visas already granted. The second check is whether Home Affairs has actually asked you. Not every applicant is automatically required to give biometrics: the Department of Home Affairs advises each applicant who must provide them and sends instructions, typically by email to the applicant or their authorised migration agent, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's report of the announcement, via PTI.

https://x.com/VFSGlobal/status/2115673127523057698

Check Two: Wait for the Letter Before Booking

The most common mistake will be booking too early. Applicants should wait until they receive an official biometrics requirement letter before booking an appointment or attempting to use the app, the High Commission said. Home Affairs' biometrics page is the official reference for the programme. The letter carries your Visa Lodgement Number, and its first three letters decide your route.

Check Three: AUI Means App, Anything Else Means a Centre

If the Visa Lodgement Number on your letter starts with AUI, you can provide your passport details and a live facial image through the Australian Immi App instead of travelling to a centre. Home Affairs' Australian Immi App guidance lists India among the countries where the app is available, and says ImmiAccount is updated within 24 hours of a successful submission. The app route is free for eligible applicants who have previously provided biometrics at a collection centre and hold a valid passport. If your VLN does not start with AUI, you must attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre in person. There are 16 centres across India, managed by VFS Global, and the centre charges a service fee.

Checks Four and Five: Passport and Phone Readiness

Both routes run on the passport linked to your application, so check it is valid before you start. For the app route, Home Affairs says your phone needs a steady internet connection, NFC switched on to read the passport chip, and camera and location access enabled. In the app you enter or scan the VLN, scan the passport data page and chip, confirm the details, take a photo against a plain, light-coloured wall, and submit. Each family member has their own VLN, so use the correct number for each person.

Why Australia Is Doing This

The High Commission said biometrics provide a reliable way to verify identity, helping protect legitimate applicants from identity misuse, reduce fraud and strengthen the integrity of Australia's migration system. Biometric information is collected, stored and managed in accordance with Australian legislation and applicable local laws, with encrypted transmission, it said. It also clarified that buying optional services from a service provider does not influence processing times or the outcome of an application. Biometric collection is not expected to affect processing times, provided applicants complete the requirement promptly after notification.

What to Do Next

If you lodged before October 26, do nothing — the change does not reach your application. If you are lodging now, apply as usual, then watch the email address on your application and your ImmiAccount for the biometrics letter, act on it promptly when it arrives, and follow only instructions issued by the Department of Home Affairs through official websites.

steps.detail: Scan the barcode on your requirement letter or type the code in. It must start with AUI.

steps.step: Scan your passport data page and chip
steps.detail: Turn on NFC first, remove your phone cover, and hold the phone over the open passport until the outline turns green.
Review the details the app read from your passport. Rescan if anything does not match.

steps.step: Take your photo in the app
steps.detail: Stand against a plain, light-coloured wall, face the camera with eyes open and visible, and remove glasses if practical.
Home Affairs says ImmiAccount updates within 24 hours. You do not need to attend a collection centre after a successful submission.
